prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1402; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a rear-end collision in which our insured's vehicle was struck from behind while stopped at a traffic signal. The claimant has retained counsel, and all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report, which records the claimant as a passenger in the vehicle at the time of impact. The report and the statements of two independent witnesses are consistent with the account given at first notice.

Entry 3: Spoke with the at-fault driver, who acknowledged responsibility and described the impact in the same terms as the witnesses. Photographs taken at the scene show rear-end damage that is largely in line with the reported force of impact.

Entry 4: Received the claimant's injury notice through counsel, describing neck pain and stiffness consistent with whiplash. The mechanism of injury appears well matched to the kind and force of the crash.

Entry 5: Confirmed with the policy records that the driver involved is listed as a named driver on the policy, and that the policy was in force at the time of loss with no coverage gap.

Entry 6: Checked the vehicle history and prior claims database. No earlier damage to the vehicle is on file, and nothing suggests the damage predates the policy's effective date.

Entry 7: Recorded the claimant's account in a recorded call with counsel present. The details matched the earlier description given at first notice, and the claimant has given the same account in every conversation so far.

Entry 8: Reviewed the medical records provided through counsel. The treatment followed a usual course of care and tapered as the claimant's condition improved. No prior injury to the same body area is known from the records or from the claimant's history.

Entry 9: Obtained the repair estimate and the appraiser's inspection notes. The damage is mostly consistent with the described impact, and the repair scope has been reviewed line by line with the appraiser.

Entry 10: Followed up with the treating provider's office to confirm billing and treatment dates. The billing lines match the records and the expected course of treatment for this type of injury.

Entry 11: Spoke with counsel to review the status of treatment and the demand package. Counsel confirmed the claimant's recovery is progressing and that treatment is winding down.

Entry 12: Updated the reserve to reflect the current treatment status and repair scope. The file is on track for evaluation, with no open coverage questions at this time.
